# Reverse braking model consumes live reverse thruster values

**Parent:** AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9 · **Issue type:** task · **Priority:** medium

## Goal

Reverse braking must be gated and modelled with the live reverse values:
`asteroidsReverseEnabled` (already respected at snapshot level),
`asteroidsReverseThrustAcceleration` and `asteroidsReverseMaxSpeed` feed the
reverse forward-model instead of being absent.

As a player who re-tuned or disabled my reverse thruster, I want the bot's
reverse braking to use my configured acceleration and speed cap, so the demo
never contradicts the handling I experience.

## Scope

- Feed the live reverse acceleration and/or reverse speed cap into the reverse
  forward-model (brake distance under reverse acceleration and/or reverse
  speed cap).
- Keep the existing `mayReverse` tuning gates (`reverseImminentOvershootGap`,
  `reverseRetreatRange`) as tunables.
- Preserve the trouble/correction semantics from AH-0MV2WJSY70070HK2 (reverse
  is not a general positioning tool).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The reverse forward-model consumes `asteroidsReverseThrustAcceleration` and/or `asteroidsReverseMaxSpeed` from the snapshot to model reverse-assisted braking distance / reverse speed cap, instead of omitting reverse physics entirely.
- Reverse remains gated on the snapshot's live `reverseEnabled`, and the existing `mayReverse` tuning gates (`reverseImminentOvershootGap`, `reverseRetreatRange`) remain tunables.
- The reverse-reserved-for-trouble/correction semantics of AH-0MV2WJSY70070HK2 are preserved (no reverse used for routine positioning).
- Unit tests cover a custom reverse config changing the reverse decision versus defaults, and reverse-disabled behaviour emitting no reverse.

## Key Files

- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts` — `mayReverse` / reverse forward-model.
- `src/ai/botSnapshot.ts` — reverse fields consumed.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts` — reverse gate/default docs.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.test.ts` — custom reverse config + disabled tests.

## Dependencies

- Depends on the live thruster-config snapshot child.
- Depends on the test-harness child.
- Related: AH-0MV2WJSY70070HK2 (reverse overuse semantics).

## Out of scope

- A full reverse-kinematics rework beyond the live numeric consumption.

## References

- Parent intake brief: AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9
- AH-0MV2JS18K006YU35 (reverse enable-flag plumbing)

## Goal

Test-first verification for collecting balance statistics from human play sessions (parent AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN, AC5). Establish the failing tests that pin the pure helper's contract and both dev-tool paths before implementation, so the collection code is driven by tests.

**User story:** As a maintainer, I want the human balance-statistics collection to be pinned by tests (pure helper + both tool paths + dev-only enforcement), so a regression in the shared extraction path is caught immediately.

## Scope

- Pure helper unit tests (single run, multiple runs, empty stream, seed attribution, determinism).
- Tool-path tests: `npm run record` emits the human `BalanceReport` artifact; `npm run evaluate --human` emits it under `--out`.
- A dev-only enforcement test asserting no production call site collects via the new path.
- A cross-path equivalence test asserting the human helper and the bot batch path share `extractBalanceStats`/`aggregateBalanceStats` and `BALANCE_STATISTICS_SCHEMA_VERSION`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Unit tests cover the pure helper: single run, multiple runs (per-run entries + one aggregate), empty stream, seed attribution from `run_header`, and deterministic (byte-stable) output.
2. Tool-path tests assert `npm run record` writes the human `BalanceReport` artifact and `npm run evaluate -- --human <file>` emits the human `BalanceReport` under `--out`.
3. A test asserts the human balance-collection path is dev-tooling only: no production (non-`scripts/`) import or call site invokes it.
4. A cross-path equivalence test asserts the human helper and the bot batch path share the same schema version and the same `extractBalanceStats`/`aggregateBalanceStats` implementation.
5. Tests are written first (fail before implementation) and pass after; the full project test suite passes via `/skill:test`.

## Key Files

- `src/ai/eval/humanStats.test.ts` (new)
- `src/ai/eval/cli.test.ts`
- `scripts/recording-cli.test.ts`
- `scripts/evaluate-args.test.ts`

- Parent: AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN
- Shared schema: AH-0MV81YJQP008L9CQ

data.title: Human balance-statistics test suite

data.description:
## Goal

Add the single shared pure helper that converts a recorded human session's flat telemetry record stream into per-run `BalanceRunStats` plus a `BalanceAggregate`, packaged as a `BalanceReport` labelled with a `human` pseudo-policy (parent AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN, AC1/AC2/AC4).

**User story:** As a maintainer, I want a pure helper that turns a recorded human session into the same balance statistics the bot framework produces, so I can compare the bot's experience against a real player's on one shared schema.

## Desired Change

1. New module `src/ai/eval/humanStats.ts` exporting a pure helper that splits a flat `TelemetryRecord[]` stream at `run_header` boundaries and attributes each run's records to its `runSeed`.
2. Reduce each run through `extractBalanceStats` (default `dtSeconds = 1/60`) and aggregate via `aggregateBalanceStats`/`createBalanceAggregator`.
3. Package the result with `buildBalanceReport` as a `kind: 'balance'` report with `policies: ['human']`.
4. Export the helper from `src/ai/eval/index.ts`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A single shared pure, clock-free and I/O-free helper exists in `src/ai/eval/humanStats.ts` and is exported from `src/ai/eval/index.ts`.
2. The helper splits a flat telemetry record stream at `run_header` boundaries and produces one `BalanceRunStats` per recorded run (seed attributed from the header).
3. It aggregates all per-run statistics into exactly one `BalanceAggregate` via `aggregateBalanceStats`/`createBalanceAggregator`, using the shared `BALANCE_STATISTICS_SCHEMA_VERSION` — no schema duplication.
4. It packages the output with `buildBalanceReport` as a `kind: 'balance'` `BalanceReport` labelled with the `human` pseudo-policy, directly comparable to bot reports.
5. An empty stream yields a deterministic, well-formed report (zero runs, empty aggregate) without throwing.
6. Output is deterministic and byte-stable via the existing stable serialisation.

## Key Files

- `src/ai/eval/humanStats.ts` (new)
- `src/ai/eval/index.ts`
- `src/ai/eval/humanStats.test.ts`
- `src/ai/eval/report.ts` (reuse `buildBalanceReport`)
- `src/ai/eval/metrics.ts` (reuse `extractBalanceStats`/`aggregateBalanceStats`)

## Related Work

- Parent: AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN
- Schema: AH-0MV81YJQP008L9CQ

## Goal

Wire `scripts/record-session.mjs` (`npm run record`) to write a human `BalanceReport` artifact next to the recording, using the shared helper (parent AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN, AC3/AC4).

**User story:** As a maintainer, I want `npm run record` to also produce the balance statistics for the session I just played, so I do not need a second tool run to obtain them.

## Desired Change

1. After writing the `.jsonl` recording, load the TS core via Vite SSR (as `scripts/evaluate.mjs` does) and invoke the shared human helper on the recorded stream.
2. Write a `balance-stats.json` artifact next to the recording (or under the requested output location), serialised byte-stably.
3. Surface the artifact path in the human and `--json` summary output.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `npm run record` writes a `balance-stats.json` human `BalanceReport` artifact next to the `.jsonl` recording (or under the requested output location).
2. The artifact is produced via the shared human helper (no divergent extraction logic) and the TS core is loaded via Vite SSR.
3. A recording containing multiple runs yields per-run `BalanceRunStats` entries plus one aggregate in the artifact.
4. The summary (text and `--json`) reports the artifact path.
5. No production telemetry/consent config or production call site changes — dev tooling only; no PII.

## Key Files

- `scripts/record-session.mjs`
- `scripts/record-session.d.mts`
- `scripts/recording-cli.test.ts`
- `src/ai/eval/humanStats.ts` (consume)

## Related Work

- Parent: AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN

## Goal

Wire `scripts/evaluate.mjs` + `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` so `--human <file>` emits the same human `BalanceReport` artifact under `--out`, as a thin shell over the shared helper (parent AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN, AC3/AC4).

**User story:** As a maintainer, I want the existing `--human` evaluation run to also emit the shared balance statistics, so the bot-vs-human comparison covers the balance schema as well as the same-seed metrics.

## Desired Change

1. In `executeEvaluation`, when `humanRecordingText` is present, parse the recording into a flat record stream and call the shared human helper.
2. Add the resulting `BalanceReport` as an artifact (e.g. `human-balance-report.json`) under `--out`.
3. Keep the existing same-seed metric comparison and ghost SVG unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `npm run evaluate -- --human <file.jsonl> --out <dir>` emits a human `BalanceReport` artifact (e.g. `human-balance-report.json`) under `--out`.
2. The artifact is produced by the shared helper and uses the `BalanceReport` shape with `policy: 'human'`.
3. The existing same-seed metric comparison (`comparison.json`) and ghost SVG (`ghost.svg`) are unchanged.
4. A recording containing multiple runs yields per-run entries plus one aggregate in the artifact.
5. Dev-tooling only: no production call site and no PII.

## Key Files

- `src/ai/eval/cli.ts`
- `scripts/evaluate.mjs`
- `src/ai/eval/cli.test.ts`
- `scripts/evaluate-args.test.ts`
- `src/ai/eval/humanStats.ts` (consume)
